fields.entry: Every story ever told lies in one bottomless manuscript, scraped thin and written over. Nobody has seen its binding.
The Ur-Text is the first draft under every page: all axioms at 5, nothing contradicts. Who wrote it is the one question no text in the game answers.
Each genre has one Author, its patron (Canon §16.5). Authors wrote their genres and then stopped; they answer prayers but never appear in person.
When a story wears thin it is scraped and overwritten. The scraping is weather, not malice.
The Style is the rule that every page agree with itself. It is not a being. The Editors serve it.
Characters who slipped through the knife when their page was scraped. They remember one genre and can hold any other's tools.
The Editors' correcting fluid. It erases what it touches; drunk, it lets an Erratum correct the world (doc 04 Marginalia powers) at the price of becoming visible to every Editor (Canon §11.6).
The blank edge of the page, where Errata gather between descents and where no Editor has jurisdiction.
Notes written past the last page. Beyond the Ur-Text there is only margin, and Errata may keep writing there.
The sign-off at the end of every page, where the scribe rests. Editors respect a signed page; a Colophon defaced by Errata is treated as forged, and an Editor waits at every later one (Canon §17.1).
The Censor keeps an office of junior redactors. When a party leaves its page open (Canon §17.9), another reader can borrow a desk and a red pen for one page.

fields.look_and_voice: widow's black, magnifier on a chain; dry, precise
fields.sample_line: "Another specimen. Do try to bring the whole thing next time."

fields.look_and_voice: thimbles on every finger, a needle behind one ear; warm, brisk
fields.sample_line: "Quires in, pages out. Mind the glue."

fields.look_and_voice: a courtesy android with a cracked faceplate; polite, literal
fields.sample_line: "Memory located. Shall I play it back for you?"

fields.look_and_voice: surveyor's chain and a blank map; laconic
fields.sample_line: "Map's blank till you walk it. Then it's mine."

fields.look_and_voice: ink to the elbows, eyes like wet print; soft, unhurried
fields.sample_line: "The well gives what it gives. Every chance is written on the rim."

fields.look_and_voice: tonsure, red-and-black ink pots; cheerful pedant
fields.sample_line: "Another page done. I'll rule the next line for you."

fields.look_and_voice: goggles, a ledger and a cart; blunt and fair
old swordsman in plain robes; spare
fields.sample_line: "Again. Slower. Now the same, but correctly."
